clue.text: Instructed old king and old socialist

parts.note: Tut is Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh of ancient Egypt
red is the colour, and so the nickname, of a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A historian lectured on an ancient monarch and a left-wing veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor gives teaching, so being taught by one is a synonym for having been instructed.

clue.text: Top CIA agent initially mixed pudding

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred together into a new order
initially takes just the opening letter of agent

explanation.surface: The head of the CIA's spy first stirred up a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a milk pudding made with starch pearls from cassava, a British school dinner classic.

clue.text: Headdress so long one wears

indicators.note: the farewell wears the numeral, which it has on it, so it holds it

parts.note: ta-ra is informal northern English for goodbye
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A goodbye to a long-worn crown.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a jewelled ornamental crown worn by a woman on formal occasions.

clue.text: Heroic animal runs home to young Belgian adventurer

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
in means at home
Tintin is the boy reporter of Hergé's Belgian comics

explanation.surface: A brave dog races back to the boy hero of a Belgian comic.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the German shepherd dog star of early Hollywood films, an animal hero.

clue.text: Doctor round surgery to wilt

parts.note: O is round in shape
op is short for operation, surgery

explanation.surface: A GP does the rounds of the practice until worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or hang limply, like a wilting plant.

clue.text: Left Dave struggling to contain lion?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold another piece within them, as a container holds its contents
Dave struggling means his letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a lion is a big cat, the question mark flagging an example

explanation.surface: Dave fled, failing to keep a lion under control.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the lion as just one example of a cat; 'struggling' gives VAED from the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacate a place is to leave it empty, so vacated is a synonym for left in the past tense.

clue.text: One unofficially upholding law leaving it in ruins

indicators.note: ruins means wreckage, so the letters lie broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-appointed lawman leaves the place devastated.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-appointed enforcer who punishes wrongdoers without legal authority.

clue.text: Crumbs US soldier gives dog

parts.note: crumbs and cor are both British exclamations of surprise
GI is an American enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier feeds crumbs to a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short-legged Welsh breed, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II, so an example of a dog.

clue.text: Firm line taken in balancing act

parts.note: tight means firm or secure
a rope is a line, especially on a ship

explanation.surface: A company's line has been drawn into a delicate compromise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a business, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively it means a delicate situation needing careful balance, from the circus high wire.

clue.text: Poem sung in act held up

indicators.note: the poem goes in the act, inside it

parts.note: a deed is an act
a lay is a narrative poem meant to be sung

explanation.surface: A ballad performed during a show is put back.
explanation.definitionFit: Delayed means postponed or late, a synonym for held up.

clue.text: Unlovely boy good for church music

parts.note: a plain person is unattractive, not lovely
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: An unattractive lad is nonetheless a fine choirboy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainchant, the unaccompanied liturgical melody sung in medieval worship, is music of the church.

clue.text: Dignified knocking beer back

indicators.note: in knocking back, back tells us to read the drink's letters from right to left

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone stays dignified while downing a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking beer back' reads as drinking, but only 'back' does work: LAGER backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal bearing is kingly and stately, so it is a synonym for dignified.

clue.text: Arab seen in Romania

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the country's name, sitting within it

explanation.surface: An Arab traveller is spotted in Eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula, so a person from there is an Arab.

clue.text: Male is taken in by worthless fortune-telling

indicators.note: the first pieces are taken inside the word for worthless, which surrounds them

parts.note: paltry means trivial or of no value

explanation.surface: A man is duped by a fortune-teller's worthless reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the lines of the hand to predict the future is a form of fortune-telling.

clue.text: Military command: go after crippled U-boat

indicators.note: the word for go comes after the shuffled letters
a crippled vessel is wrecked, so the submarine's letters are broken up

parts.note: a go or turn is a person's opportunity in a game

explanation.surface: An order is barked as a stricken submarine is pursued.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in U-boat is ignored, so 'crippled' works on five letters; 'after' sets the go word last.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the drill order to face the opposite direction, a command on the parade ground.

clue.text: Domestic support for alumnus on the look-out

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting word sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: OB means old boy, a former pupil
a domestic is a household servant

explanation.surface: A former pupil's home help stays watchful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and quick to notice things is the same as being watchful.

clue.text: Sun terribly mischievous or concerned for others?

indicators.note: terribly suggests a mess, so the three letters are scrambled

parts.note: elfish means impish, like a mischievous elf

explanation.surface: Asks whether a newspaper is wickedly prankish or genuinely caring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, which makes the surface read like media criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking of others before oneself is what selflessness means.

clue.text: Admonish Charlie, flogged outside

indicators.note: the word for flogged goes outside, wrapping around the letter

parts.note: to flog is informal for to sell
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Reprimand a boy called Charlie who has been beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' looks like a beating but means sold, British slang for selling.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone is to rebuke them angrily, a synonym for admonish.

clue.text: Extra weight that's in the boot?

definitions.meaning: a roll of fat around the waist
the reserve wheel kept in a car's trunk, which the British call the boot

explanation.surface: Asks where some surplus heft is stored.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both belly fat and the reserve wheel carried in a car.

clue.text: Ascetic's last to leave German city

indicators.note: the final letter of the ascetic's name departs

parts.note: an Essene was a member of an ascetic Jewish sect of ancient times

explanation.surface: A hermit is the final one to depart from a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to leave' removes the final E of ESSENE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Ransacked in Roma: pie shops

indicators.note: ransacked means turned upside down, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Bakeries in Rome have been looted for pies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin plural of emporium, a large store, gives a word for shops.

clue.text: Cry, having cut gathering fruit

indicators.note: the word for cut gathers the fruit into its middle

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as wool from sheep
a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: Someone weeps after cutting themselves while picking fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' looks like harvesting fruit, but it is the container signal; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed a tear is an idiom meaning to weep, so it can stand for cry as a verb.

clue.text: Intend to appear in torn dress

indicators.note: the word for intend appears within the word for torn

parts.note: rent means torn apart
to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Someone means to turn up in a ripped frock.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing, so it means dress as a noun.

clue.text: Case for governmental responsibility

definitions.meaning: a flat carrying case for papers or drawings
the area of business assigned to a minister, such as finance

explanation.surface: Arguing the case for a government taking responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flat document case and a minister's area of duties.

clue.text: Great lump taken from turf at source

indicators.note: the letters are lifted out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A big clod of earth has been cut from the original turf.
explanation.definitionFit: An insulting name for a fat person, someone called a big lump.

clue.text: Some get a rollicking over talk

indicators.note: over tells us to turn the picked letters right over, backwards
some means only part of the following words are used

explanation.surface: Some people are given a telling-off after a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ETARO from 'get a rollicking' and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to give a formal speech, a verb meaning to talk.

clue.text: Nasty bug from priest keeping company

indicators.note: the priest keeps the company within him

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A cleric picks up a horrible infection from the people around him.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bacterium causing food poisoning, so it is fairly called a nasty bug.

clue.text: City in South Africa in fine area

indicators.note: the second in places the country's letters inside the word for fine

parts.note: OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: A city in South Africa sits in a pleasant district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City in South Africa' looks like the place's location, but the city is in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major port city in Japan, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Criticise severely when stopping nonsense

indicators.note: the small word stops up the nonsense, plugging its middle

parts.note: rot is rubbish or nonsense
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Tear into someone harshly when they halt the drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is informal for berating or mocking them mercilessly.

clue.text: Canine, say, barking regardless

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A dog, for instance, keeps barking no matter what.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' fits the dog but means crazy, an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an adverbial idiom meaning anyway, whatever happens.

clue.text: Opponent takes over church in ancient city

parts.note: an anti is someone opposed to something
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: An adversary seizes control of a church in an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a major city of the ancient Hellenistic world, in present-day Turkey.

clue.text: Stylish English worker holding on

indicators.note: the English worker together holds the word for on inside it

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker
on is the leg side in cricket, so on gives leg

explanation.surface: An English labourer clinging on is surprisingly chic.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful and refined in appearance, which is a synonym for stylish.
